newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SM Prime to open more shopping malls.
newsitem.headline: SM Prime to open more shopping malls.

text.p: The Philippine's largest retail chain operator, SM Prime Holdings Inc, said on Wednesday it planned to open more malls to meet the increasingly wealthy population's desire to shop.

"The times are very exciting for the shopping mall industry. With the country's bullish economic growth, people have more purchasing power and more discriminating taste," SM Prime chairman Henry Sy told shareholders in in their annual meeting.
"We expect the retail industry to grow between 12 and 15 percent annually from now up to the year 2000," senior vice president Jose Sio said.
Sy said SM Prime is opening two new malls each year in the next five yars.
The shopping mall operator is opening one mall each in Manila's Quezon district and another in Cavite province, south of the capital in July.
SM Prime will open another mall in Manila next year and one more in the central Iloilo province.

The retailer has 154 hectares of undeveloped land around the country, reserved for future shopping malls. The proposed projects include one shopping mall each in the southern Davao city and in Bacolod and Tacloban cities in central Philippines.
It currently operates five shopping malls -- four in Metro Manila and one in Cebu in central Philippines.
SM Prime will pour between three and 3.5 billion pesos from previous earnings for capital expenditures and land acquisition this year, Sio said.

He was confident the SM malls would continue to attract shoppers despite growing competition from new mall operators and a proposal in Congress to open up the local retail industry to foreign investors.
Under Philippine laws, only Filipinos can engage in the local retail business.
SM Prime expects to post a net income of 2.4 billion pesos this year from 1.9 billion in 1996.
